chapters.title: A Song for the King
chapters.html:
Psalms 45

For the director: on "Lilies." Of the sons of Korah. A Maskil. A love song.

1My heart overflows with a good word;
I speak my verses to the king;
my tongue is the pen of a skillful scribe.

2You are the most handsome of the sons of men;
grace is poured on your lips;
therefore God has blessed you forever.

3Gird your sword on your thigh, mighty one,
your splendor and your majesty.

4In your majesty ride on victoriously
for the cause of truth and humility and righteousness;
let your right hand teach you fearsome deeds.

5Your arrows are sharp;
peoples fall under you;
they fall in the heart of the king's enemies.

6Your throne, O God, is forever and ever;
the scepter of your kingdom is a scepter of uprightness.

7You have loved righteousness and hated wickedness;
therefore God, your God, has anointed you
with the oil of gladness above your companions.

8All your robes are myrrh and aloes and cassia;
from palaces of ivory, stringed instruments make you glad.

9Daughters of kings are among your honored women;
at your right hand stands the queen in gold of Ophir.

10Listen, daughter, and see, and incline your ear:
forget your people and your father's house,

11and the king will desire your beauty.
Since he is your lord, bow down to him.

12The daughter of Tyre will come with a gift;
the richest of the people will seek your favor.

13All glorious is the king's daughter within;
her clothing is woven with gold.

14In embroidered robes she is led to the king,
with the young women, her companions, following her;
they are brought to you.

15With joy and gladness they are led along;
they enter the palace of the king.

16In place of your fathers will be your sons;
you will make them princes in all the earth.

17I will make your name remembered in all generations;
therefore peoples will praise you forever and ever.

Notes

  • The title "on 'Lilies'… A love song" — al shoshannim, the name of a tune (69, 80); shir yedidot, a song of loves, for a royal wedding.

  • v1 "my tongue is the pen of a skillful scribe" — et sofer mahir, as Ezra was a skilled scribe (Ezra 7:6).

  • v2 "grace is poured on your lips" — the king's gracious speech (Proverbs 22:11; Luke 4:22).

  • v6 "Your throne, O God, is forever and ever" — the king addressed as Elohim, God, as rulers are called gods in 82:6; the line may also be read Your throne is God's, forever and ever, or your divine throne. Hebrews 1:8–9 quotes vv6–7 of the Son: Your throne, O God, is forever and ever. The psalm is rendered as the Old Testament has it, with the king in lowercase.

  • v7 "God, your God, has anointed you" — the king anointed with the oil of gladness, above the other kings; Messiah means Anointed (2:2).

  • v8 "myrrh and aloes and cassia" — the spices of the wedding garments (Song of Songs 4:14; John 19:39). Palaces of ivory: rooms paneled with ivory, as Ahab's house (1 Kings 22:39; Amos 3:15).

  • v9 "the queen in gold of Ophir" — the bride, shegal, the queen consort (Nehemiah 2:6).

  • vv10–11 "forget your people and your father's house" — the foreign bride leaves her own people, as Ruth did (Ruth 1:16; Genesis 2:24).

  • v13 "All glorious is the king's daughter within" — penimah, inside the palace, in her chamber before the procession.

  • v17 "therefore peoples will praise you forever" — the Church has sung the psalm of Christ and His bride, the Church; the Ethiopian Church also sings it of the Virgin Mary, the queen at the King's right hand.

chapters.title: God Is Our Refuge and Strength
chapters.html:
Psalms 46

For the director. Of the sons of Korah. On Alamoth. A song.

1God is our refuge and strength,
a help in trouble, found very near.

2Therefore we will not fear though the earth gives way,
though the mountains slip into the heart of the seas,

3though its waters roar and foam,
though the mountains tremble at its swelling. Selah

4There is a river whose streams make glad the city of God,
the holy dwelling place of the Most High.

5God is within her; she will not be moved;
God will help her at the break of morning.

6Nations rage; kingdoms totter;
He lifts His voice; the earth melts.

7The LORD of hosts is with us;
the God of Jacob is our fortress. Selah

8Come, see the works of the LORD,
who has brought desolations on the earth.

9He makes wars cease to the end of the earth;
He breaks the bow and snaps the spear;
He burns the chariots with fire.

10"Be still, and know that I am God.
I will be exalted among the nations;
I will be exalted in the earth."

11The LORD of hosts is with us;
the God of Jacob is our fortress. Selah

Notes

  • The title "On Alamoth" — al alamot, for young women, perhaps for high voices (1 Chronicles 15:20).

  • vv2–3 — the world returning to chaos, the mountains sinking back into the waters (Genesis 1:2, 9); even then God's people need not fear.

  • v4 "There is a river" — Jerusalem had no river, only the spring of Gihon; the river is the river of God's presence, the river of Your delights (36:8; Ezekiel 47:1–12; Revelation 22:1–2).

  • v5 "at the break of morning" — lifnot boqer, the hour of rescue, as when the Assyrian army lay dead at dawn (Isaiah 37:36).

  • vv7, 11 "The LORD of hosts is with us" — YHWH tseva'ot immanu: immanu, with us, the word of Immanuel, God with us (Isaiah 7:14; 8:8–10).

  • v9 "He burns the chariots with fire" — agalot, wagons; the Greek reads shields. The end of war is the end of the weapons of war (Isaiah 2:4).

  • v10 "Be still, and know that I am God" — harpu, let go, stop: God speaks to the raging nations (v6), and to His people.

  • v1 and the hymn — the psalm is the source of Luther's A Mighty Fortress Is Our God.

chapters.title: God Has Gone Up with a Shout
chapters.html:
Psalms 47

For the director. Of the sons of Korah. A psalm.

1Clap your hands, all you peoples;
shout to God with the voice of joy.

2For the LORD, the Most High, is to be feared,
a great King over all the earth.

3He subdued peoples under us,
and nations under our feet.

4He chose our inheritance for us,
the pride of Jacob, whom He loves. Selah

5God has gone up with a shout,
the LORD with the sound of the horn.

6Sing praises to God, sing praises;
sing praises to our King, sing praises.

7For God is the King of all the earth;
sing praises with a Maskil.

8God reigns over the nations;
God sits on His holy throne.

9The nobles of the peoples have gathered
as the people of the God of Abraham.
For the shields of the earth belong to God;
He is highly exalted.

Notes

  • The psalm — a hymn to God as King of all the earth, perhaps sung as the ark was carried up to the temple (24:7–10; 2 Samuel 6:15).

  • v1 "Clap your hands, all you peoples" — the clapping and shouting of a coronation (2 Kings 11:12).

  • v4 "the pride of Jacob" — the land of promise, Israel's glory (Amos 6:8; Nahum 2:2).

  • v5 "God has gone up with a shout" — alah, gone up, to His throne; the horn, shofar, sounded at the crowning of a king (1 Kings 1:39). The Church sings the psalm at the feast of the Ascension.

  • vv6–7 "Sing praises" — zammeru, five times in two verses.

  • v7 "sing praises with a Maskil" — maskil, the word of the psalm titles (32), here perhaps a skillful song.

  • v9 "as the people of the God of Abraham" — the nations gathered as God's people, the promise to Abraham fulfilled: in you all the families of the earth shall be blessed (Genesis 12:3). The shields of the earth are its rulers (89:18).

chapters.title: The City of the Great King
chapters.html:
Psalms 48

A song. A psalm of the sons of Korah.

1Great is the LORD and greatly to be praised
in the city of our God, His holy mountain.

2Beautiful in height, the joy of all the earth,
is Mount Zion, the heights of the north,
the city of the great King.

3In her citadels God
has made Himself known as a stronghold.

4For the kings assembled;
they came on together.

5They saw it, and they were astounded;
they were terrified; they fled in haste.

6Trembling took hold of them there,
anguish as of a woman in labor,

7as when the east wind
shatters the ships of Tarshish.

8As we have heard, so we have seen
in the city of the LORD of hosts, in the city of our God;
God will establish her forever. Selah

9We have pondered Your loyal love, God,
within Your temple.

10As Your name, God,
so Your praise reaches to the ends of the earth;
Your right hand is full of righteousness.

11Let Mount Zion be glad;
let the daughters of Judah rejoice
because of Your judgments.

12Walk around Zion, go all around her;
count her towers;

13set your heart on her ramparts;
go through her citadels,
so that you may tell the generation to come

14that this is God,
our God forever and ever;
He will guide us beyond death.

Notes

  • The psalm — a song of Zion, the city where God dwells (46; 76; 84; 87; 122).

  • v2 "the heights of the north" — yarketei tsafon, the far north, where the mountain of the gods was said to stand in the old Canaanite poems (Isaiah 14:13); here Zion is that mountain. The city of the great King is quoted by Jesus (Matthew 5:35).

  • vv4–7 "the kings assembled… they fled in haste" — an attack on Jerusalem broken by God, as at the time of Hezekiah (2 Kings 19:35–36).

  • v6 "anguish as of a woman in labor" — the image of sudden, helpless terror (Jeremiah 6:24).

  • v7 "the ships of Tarshish" — the great sea-going ships of the far west (1 Kings 10:22; Isaiah 2:16), wrecked by the east wind (Ezekiel 27:26).

  • v8 "As we have heard, so we have seen" — what the fathers told of God's deeds (44:1) the worshipers now see in the city.

  • vv12–13 "Walk around Zion… count her towers" — the procession around the walls, a tour of the city's strength to be told to the next generation.

  • v14 "He will guide us beyond death" — al mut, over death, or to the end; some read it as a musical direction belonging to the next psalm, al mut, as in the title of Psalm 9. The Greek has forever.

chapters.title: No Man Can Ransom Another
chapters.html:
Psalms 49

For the director. Of the sons of Korah. A psalm.

1Hear this, all you peoples;
listen, all who live in the world,

2both low and high,
rich and poor together.

3My mouth will speak wisdom;
the meditation of my heart will be understanding.

4I will incline my ear to a proverb;
I will open my riddle on the lyre.

5Why should I fear in days of trouble,
when the iniquity of those who dog my heels surrounds me,

6those who trust in their wealth
and boast of the abundance of their riches?

7Truly no man can ransom his brother
or give to God the price of his life,

8for the ransom of their soul is costly,
and it must be given up forever,

9that he should live on forever
and never see the pit.

10For he sees that even the wise die;
the fool and the stupid alike perish
and leave their wealth to others.

11Their graves are their homes forever,
their dwellings to all generations,
though they named lands after themselves.

12Man in his splendor does not stay the night;
he is like the beasts that perish.

13This is the way of those who have foolish confidence,
and of those after them who approve their words. Selah

14Like sheep they are appointed for Sheol;
death will shepherd them,
and the upright will rule over them in the morning;
their form will waste away in Sheol, far from their dwelling.

15But God will ransom my soul from the hand of Sheol,
for He will take me. Selah

16Do not be afraid when a man becomes rich,
when the glory of his house increases.

17For when he dies he will take nothing away;
his glory will not go down after him.

18Though while he lives he counts his soul blessed,
and men praise you when you do well for yourself,

19he will go to the generation of his fathers,
who will never again see the light.

20Man in his splendor, without understanding,
is like the beasts that perish.

Notes

  • The psalm — a wisdom poem, a riddle (v4) on death and riches, addressed to all peoples like the book of Proverbs.

  • v5 "those who dog my heels" — avon aqevai, the iniquity of my heels, of those who lie in wait at my heels (56:6).

  • vv7–9 "no man can ransom his brother" — kofer, the ransom price of a life (Exodus 21:30); for death no ransom is enough. What shall a man give in return for his soul? (Mark 8:37).

  • v11 "Their graves are their homes forever" — the Greek and Syriac read qivram, their graves; the Hebrew has qirbam, their inward thought: their inward thought is that their houses are forever. The witnesses are followed here.

  • vv12, 20 — the refrain differs by one letter: v12 bal yalin, does not stay the night; v20 ve-lo yavin, without understanding.

  • v14 "death will shepherd them" — death as the shepherd of the wicked, against the LORD is my shepherd (23:1). The rest of the verse is very hard.

  • v15 "for He will take me" — yiqqacheni, the verb used of Enoch, God took him (Genesis 5:24), and of Elijah (2 Kings 2:3): the hope of life with God beyond Sheol (73:24).

  • v17 "when he dies he will take nothing away" — we brought nothing into the world, and we cannot take anything out (1 Timothy 6:7; Job 1:21).

chapters.title: God Himself Is Judge
chapters.html:
Psalms 50

A psalm of Asaph.

1The Mighty One, God, the LORD, has spoken
and summoned the earth
from the rising of the sun to its setting.

2Out of Zion, the perfection of beauty,
God shines out.

3Our God comes and does not keep silent;
before Him is a devouring fire,
and around Him a mighty storm.

4He calls to the heavens above
and to the earth, to judge His people:

5"Gather to Me My faithful ones,
who made a covenant with Me by sacrifice."

6The heavens declare His righteousness,
for God Himself is judge. Selah

7"Hear, My people, and I will speak;
Israel, I will testify against you.
I am God, your God.

8Not for your sacrifices do I rebuke you;
your burnt offerings are always before Me.

9I will not take a bull from your house
or goats from your folds.

10For every beast of the forest is Mine,
the cattle on a thousand hills.

11I know every bird of the mountains,
and all that moves in the field is Mine.

12If I were hungry, I would not tell you,
for the world and all that fills it are Mine.

13Do I eat the flesh of bulls
or drink the blood of goats?

14Offer to God a sacrifice of thanksgiving,
and pay your vows to the Most High,

15and call on Me in the day of trouble;
I will rescue you, and you will glorify Me."

16But to the wicked God says:
"What right have you to recite My statutes
or take My covenant on your lips?

17For you hate discipline
and throw My words behind you.

18When you see a thief, you are pleased with him,
and your portion is with adulterers.

19You let your mouth loose for evil,
and your tongue weaves deceit.

20You sit and speak against your brother;
you slander your own mother's son.

21These things you have done, and I kept silent;
you thought I was altogether like you.
I will rebuke you and set it out before your eyes.

22Understand this, you who forget God,
or I will tear you apart, and there will be no one to rescue.

23The one who offers thanksgiving as his sacrifice glorifies Me;
to the one who sets his way aright
I will show the salvation of God."

Notes

  • The title "A psalm of Asaph" — Asaph, David's chief musician (1 Chronicles 16:5, 7), named over Psalms 50 and 73–83.

  • v1 "The Mighty One, God, the LORD" — El Elohim YHWH, three names together, as in Joshua 22:22: the full title of the Judge who summons His court.

  • v3 "before Him is a devouring fire" — God coming as at Sinai, in fire and storm (Exodus 19:16–18; Deuteronomy 4:24).

  • v5 "who made a covenant with Me by sacrifice" — the covenant sealed with blood at Sinai (Exodus 24:5–8).

  • vv8–13 — God does not need sacrifices as food; the earth is the LORD's, and all that fills it (24:1). The fault is not the sacrifices but the hearts of those who offer them (51:16–17; 1 Samuel 15:22; Hosea 6:6).

  • v14 "a sacrifice of thanksgiving" — todah, the thank offering (Leviticus 7:12); the sacrifice of praise, the fruit of lips (Hebrews 13:15).

  • vv16–21 — the second charge, against those who recite the law and break it: theft, adultery, slander (Romans 2:21–23).

  • v21 "you thought I was altogether like you" — heyot ehyeh khamokha, with ehyeh, the verb of God's name, I AM WHO I AM (Exodus 3:14): because God was silent, they thought Him no better than themselves.

  • v22 "or I will tear you apart" — pen etrof, God as a lion (Hosea 5:14).

chapters.title: Create in Me a Clean Heart
chapters.html:
Psalms 51

For the director. A psalm of David, when Nathan the prophet came to him, after he had gone in to Bathsheba.

1Be gracious to me, God, according to Your loyal love;
according to the greatness of Your compassion, blot out my transgressions.

2Wash me thoroughly from my iniquity,
and cleanse me from my sin.

3For I know my transgressions,
and my sin is always before me.

4Against You, You only, have I sinned
and done what is evil in Your sight,
so that You are right when You speak
and blameless when You judge.

5I was brought forth in iniquity,
and in sin my mother conceived me.

6You desire truth in the inward parts,
and in the hidden place You teach me wisdom.

7Purge me with hyssop, and I will be clean;
wash me, and I will be whiter than snow.

8Let me hear joy and gladness;
let the bones You have crushed rejoice.

9Hide Your face from my sins,
and blot out all my iniquities.

10Create in me a clean heart, God,
and renew a steadfast spirit within me.

11Do not cast me away from Your presence,
and do not take Your Holy Spirit from me.

12Restore to me the joy of Your salvation,
and uphold me with a willing spirit.

13Then I will teach transgressors Your ways,
and sinners will return to You.

14Deliver me from bloodguilt, God,
the God of my salvation,
and my tongue will sing aloud of Your righteousness.

15Lord, open my lips,
and my mouth will declare Your praise.

16For You do not delight in sacrifice, or I would give it;
You are not pleased with burnt offering.

17The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit;
a broken and crushed heart, God, You will not despise.

18Do good to Zion in Your good pleasure;
build the walls of Jerusalem.

19Then You will delight in sacrifices of righteousness,
in burnt offering and whole offering;
then bulls will be offered on Your altar.

Notes

  • The title — David's repentance after Nathan's parable (2 Samuel 12:1–13); the Hebrew title takes two verses, so the Hebrew numbers run two ahead. The fourth of the penitential psalms (see 6).

  • vv1–2 "blot out… wash… cleanse" — three words for removing sin (as a debt struck out of a book, as stains scrubbed from cloth, as uncleanness purified) for the three words for sin of 32:1–2.

  • v4 "Against You, You only, have I sinned" — David had sinned against Uriah and Bathsheba, but all sin is first against God (2 Samuel 12:13; Genesis 39:9). Paul quotes the second half from the Greek, that You may be justified in Your words (Romans 3:4).

  • v5 "in sin my mother conceived me" — not a charge against his mother, but a confession that sin reaches back to the beginning of his life (58:3; Job 14:4).

  • v7 "Purge me with hyssop" — techatte'eni, un-sin me; hyssop was used to sprinkle the blood and water of cleansing (Leviticus 14:4–7; Numbers 19:18). Though your sins are like scarlet, they shall be as white as snow (Isaiah 1:18).

  • v10 "Create in me a clean heart" — bera, the verb of Genesis 1:1, used only of God's own work: a new creation (Ezekiel 36:26; 2 Corinthians 5:17).

  • v11 "Your Holy Spirit" — ruach qodshekha, capitalized as the word table has it; one of only three places in the Old Testament with this name (Isaiah 63:10–11). David remembered Saul, from whom the Spirit departed (1 Samuel 16:14).

  • v15 "Lord, open my lips" — the words that open the daily prayers of the Church.

  • vv16–17 "The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit" — as in 50:8–15 and 34:18.

  • vv18–19 — a prayer for the walls of Jerusalem, perhaps added when the city lay in ruins; then sacrifices offered rightly will please God.

chapters.title: Like a Green Olive Tree
chapters.html:
Psalms 52

For the director. A Maskil of David, when Doeg the Edomite came and told Saul, "David has come to the house of Ahimelech."

1Why do you boast of evil, mighty man?
The loyal love of God endures all day long.

2Your tongue plots ruin,
like a sharpened razor, you worker of deceit.

3You love evil more than good,
lying more than speaking what is right. Selah

4You love all words that devour,
you deceitful tongue.

5God will also break you down forever;
He will snatch you and tear you away from your tent;
He will uproot you from the land of the living. Selah

6The righteous will see and fear,
and will laugh at him:

7"Here is the man who would not make God his stronghold,
but trusted in the abundance of his riches
and grew strong in his ruin."

8But I am like a green olive tree in the house of God;
I trust in the loyal love of God forever and ever.

9I will give thanks to You forever, because You have done it;
I will wait for Your name, for it is good, in the presence of Your faithful ones.

Notes

  • The title — Doeg the Edomite, Saul's chief herdsman, saw David at Nob and told Saul, and then killed the priests of Nob at Saul's command (1 Samuel 21:7; 22:9–19). The Hebrew title takes two verses.

  • v1 "mighty man" — ha-gibbor, said in scorn: the man who is mighty in evil. Against his boasting stands the loyal love of God, chesed El, which lasts all day.

  • v2 "like a sharpened razor" — the tongue that cuts (57:4; Jeremiah 9:8); Doeg's words cost eighty-five priests their lives.

  • v5 "He will uproot you from the land of the living" — the fate the wicked man brought on others (Proverbs 2:22).

  • v6 "The righteous will see and fear, and will laugh at him" — fear of God's judgment, and laughter at the folly of the man who trusted in his wealth (2:4; Job 22:19).

  • v8 "like a green olive tree in the house of God" — rooted and long-lived, against the uprooted wicked (v5; 1:3; 92:12–14; Jeremiah 11:16).

  • v9 "I will wait for Your name" — aqavveh, the hope of 25:3 and 27:14.

chapters.title: The Fool Says in His Heart
chapters.html:
Psalms 53

For the director: on Mahalath. A Maskil of David.

1The fool says in his heart, "There is no God."
They are corrupt; they do detestable injustice;
there is no one who does good.

2God looks down from heaven on the children of man,
to see if there is anyone who understands,
who seeks God.

3They have all fallen away; together they have become corrupt;
there is no one who does good,
not even one.

4Do they have no knowledge, those who do iniquity,
who eat up my people as they eat bread,
and do not call on God?

5There they are in great terror,
where there was no terror,
for God has scattered the bones of the one who camps against you;
you have put them to shame, for God has rejected them.

6Oh that the salvation of Israel would come out of Zion!
When God restores the fortunes of His people,
let Jacob rejoice, let Israel be glad.

Notes

  • The psalm — Psalm 14 again, as the second book of the Psalms has it: God (Elohim) for the LORD (YHWH), and other changes. The English is that of Psalm 14 where the Hebrew is the same, and differs where it differs.

  • The title "on Mahalath" — al machalat, perhaps a tune, or for sickness; also over Psalm 88.

  • v1 "they do detestable injustice" — hit'ivu avel, injustice, for alilah, deeds, in 14:1. Detestable follows the word table for the root of to'evah.

  • v3 "They have all fallen away" — kullo sag, for ha-kol sar, turned aside, in 14:3.

  • v5 — quite different from 14:5–6: where there was no terror, a sudden panic in the camp of an enemy that besieged Jerusalem, and the bones of the besiegers scattered unburied (2 Kings 19:35; Ezekiel 6:5). The one who camps against you is chonakh; you have put them to shame is spoken to Israel.

  • v6 "the salvation of Israel" — yeshu'ot, salvations, plural here; singular in 14:7.

God looks down from heaven on the children of man, to see if there is anyone who understands, who seeks God.
They have all fallen away; together they have become corrupt; there is no one who does good, not even one.
Do they have no knowledge, those who do iniquity, who eat up my people as they eat bread, and do not call on God?
There they are in great terror, where there was no terror, for God has scattered the bones of the one who camps against you; you have put them to shame, for God has rejected them.
Oh that the salvation of Israel would come out of Zion! When God restores the fortunes of His people, let Jacob rejoice, let Israel be glad.

chapters.title: God Is My Helper
chapters.html:
Psalms 54

For the director: with stringed instruments. A Maskil of David, when the Ziphites came and said to Saul, "Is not David hiding among us?"

1God, save me by Your name,
and vindicate me by Your might.

2God, hear my prayer;
listen to the words of my mouth.

3For strangers have risen against me,
and ruthless men seek my life;
they have not set God before them. Selah

4God is my helper;
the Lord is among those who uphold my life.

5He will repay the evil to my enemies;
in Your faithfulness put an end to them.

6With a freewill offering I will sacrifice to You;
I will give thanks to Your name, LORD, for it is good.

7For He has delivered me from every trouble,
and my eye has looked on my enemies.

Notes

  • The title — the men of Ziph, in the wilderness of Judah, twice betrayed David's hiding place to Saul (1 Samuel 23:19; 26:1). The Hebrew title takes two verses.

  • v1 "save me by Your name" — God's name as His presence and power (20:1); vindicate me, tedineni, judge my case.

  • v3 "strangers have risen against me" — zarim; Psalm 86:14, which repeats the line, has zedim, the proud, one letter different. The Ziphites were of David's own tribe, yet acted as strangers.

  • v4 "the Lord is among those who uphold my life" — God stands with the few who are loyal to David (1 Samuel 23:16–18).

  • v5 "He will repay the evil" — the read form, yashiv; the written form yashuv, the evil will return.

  • v6 "a freewill offering" — nedavah, a sacrifice given not by vow or duty but gladly (Leviticus 7:16). LORD, YHWH, the one use of the name in this psalm.

  • v7 "my eye has looked on my enemies" — has seen their defeat (59:10; 92:11).

God, save me by Your name, and vindicate me by Your might.
God, hear my prayer; listen to the words of my mouth.
For strangers have risen against me, and ruthless men seek my life; they have not set God before them. Selah
God is my helper; the Lord is among those who uphold my life.
He will repay the evil to my enemies; in Your faithfulness put an end to them.
With a freewill offering I will sacrifice to You; I will give thanks to Your name, LORD, for it is good.
For He has delivered me from every trouble, and my eye has looked on my enemies.

chapters.title: Oh That I Had Wings Like a Dove
chapters.html:
Psalms 55

For the director: with stringed instruments. A Maskil of David.

1Give ear to my prayer, God,
and do not hide Yourself from my plea.

2Attend to me and answer me;
I am restless in my complaint, and I moan,

3because of the voice of the enemy,
because of the pressure of the wicked;
for they bring down trouble on me,
and in anger they bear a grudge against me.

4My heart writhes within me;
the terrors of death have fallen on me.

5Fear and trembling come on me,
and horror covers me.

6I said, "Oh that I had wings like a dove!
I would fly away and be at rest;

7I would wander far away;
I would lodge in the wilderness; Selah

8I would hurry to my place of refuge
from the raging wind and the storm."

9Swallow them up, Lord; divide their tongues,
for I see violence and strife in the city.

10Day and night they go around it on its walls,
and iniquity and trouble are within it;

11ruin is within it;
oppression and deceit do not depart from its square.

12For it is not an enemy who taunts me,
or I could bear it;
it is not one who hates me who exalts himself against me,
or I could hide from him.

13But it is you, a man of my own rank,
my companion, my familiar friend.

14We used to share sweet counsel together;
we walked in the house of God with the throng.

15Let death come on them by surprise;
let them go down alive to Sheol,
for evil is in their lodging, within them.

16As for me, I call to God,
and the LORD will save me.

17Evening and morning and at noon
I complain and moan,
and He hears my voice.

18He redeems my soul in peace
from the battle against me,
for many are with me.

19God will hear and humble them,
He who sits enthroned from of old, Selah
those who have no changes
and do not fear God.

20He stretched out his hand against those at peace with him;
he broke his covenant.

21His speech was smoother than butter,
but war was in his heart;
his words were softer than oil,
but they were drawn swords.

22Cast your burden on the LORD,
and He will sustain you;
He will never let the righteous be moved.

23But You, God, will bring them down
to the pit of destruction;
men of bloodshed and deceit
will not live out half their days.
But I will trust in You.

Notes

  • vv6–8 "Oh that I had wings like a dove!" — the longing to escape, as Jeremiah wished for a lodging in the desert (Jeremiah 9:2).

  • v9 "Swallow them up, Lord; divide their tongues" — balla… pallag, as at Babel, when God confused the speech of the builders (Genesis 11:7–9).

  • vv12–14 "it is not an enemy who taunts me… but it is you" — the betrayal by a close friend, as Ahithophel betrayed David (2 Samuel 15:12, 31); compare 41:9.

  • v14 "We used to share sweet counsel together" — namtiq sod, made counsel sweet, close friendship (Job 29:4).

  • v15 "Let death come on them by surprise" — the read form, yashi mavet; the written form joins the words, yeshimot, desolations. Go down alive to Sheol as Korah's company did (Numbers 16:30–33). Their lodging is megurim, from gur, the place where one lives as a guest.

  • v17 "Evening and morning and at noon" — the three times of prayer (Daniel 6:10).

  • v18 "for many are with me" — or against me; the Hebrew be-rabbim hayu immadi can mean either.

  • v19 "those who have no changes" — chalifot, no change of heart, or no reversals of fortune, and so no fear of God.

  • v22 "Cast your burden on the LORD" — yehavkha, what He has given you, your lot; casting all your anxieties on Him, because He cares for you (1 Peter 5:7).

chapters.title: In God I Trust
chapters.html:
Psalms 56

For the director: on "The Silent Dove of Far Places." Of David. A Miktam, when the Philistines seized him in Gath.

1Be gracious to me, God, for man tramples on me;
all day long the fighter presses me.

2My enemies trample on me all day long,
for many fight against me proudly.

3On the day I am afraid,
I trust in You.

4In God, whose word I praise,
in God I trust; I will not be afraid.
What can flesh do to me?

5All day long they twist my words;
all their thoughts are against me for evil.

6They stir up strife; they lurk;
they watch my heels,
as they have waited for my life.

7For their iniquity, will they escape?
In anger bring down the peoples, God.

8You have counted my wanderings;
put my tears in Your flask.
Are they not in Your book?

9Then my enemies will turn back
on the day I call.
This I know, that God is for me.

10In God, whose word I praise,
in the LORD, whose word I praise,

11in God I trust; I will not be afraid.
What can man do to me?

12Your vows are on me, God;
I will pay thank offerings to You.

13For You have delivered my soul from death,
and my feet from stumbling,
so that I may walk before God
in the light of the living.

Notes

  • The title "The Silent Dove of Far Places" — yonat elem rechoqim, the name of a tune. When the Philistines seized him in Gath: David's flight to Achish (1 Samuel 21:10–15), the occasion of Psalm 34 also.

  • v2 "proudly" — marom, on high; or a name of God, O Most High.

  • vv4, 10–11 — a refrain, In God I trust; I will not be afraid; v4 ends What can flesh do to me?, v11 What can man do to me? (118:6; Hebrews 13:6).

  • v6 "They stir up strife" — yaguru, from a second gur, to stir up, attack, not the gur of the guest (59:3).

  • v7 "will they escape?" — the Hebrew is short and hard, al aven pallet lamo, for iniquity, escape for them?

  • v8 "my wanderings… Your flask" — nodi and nodekha, a play on words: God counts every step of the fugitive (nod), and keeps every tear in His leather bottle (nod). Your book is God's record (139:16; Malachi 3:16).

  • v9 "God is for me" — Elohim li; If God is for us, who can be against us? (Romans 8:31).

  • v13 "in the light of the living" — the light of life, as against the darkness of Sheol (Job 33:30).

chapters.title: My Heart Is Steadfast
chapters.html:
Psalms 57

For the director: "Do Not Destroy." Of David. A Miktam, when he fled from Saul, in the cave.

1Be gracious to me, God, be gracious to me,
for in You my soul takes refuge;
in the shadow of Your wings I take refuge,
till the storms of ruin pass by.

2I call to God Most High,
to God who completes His work for me.

3He will send from heaven and save me;
He puts to shame the one who tramples on me. Selah
God will send out His loyal love and His truth.

4My soul is among lions;
I lie down among those who blaze,
the children of man, whose teeth are spears and arrows,
and their tongue a sharp sword.

5Be exalted above the heavens, God;
let Your glory be over all the earth.

6They prepared a net for my steps;
my soul was bowed down.
They dug a pit before me;
they have fallen into it themselves. Selah

7My heart is steadfast, God,
my heart is steadfast;
I will sing and make music.

8Wake up, my glory!
Wake up, harp and lyre!
I will wake the dawn.

9I will give thanks to You, Lord, among the peoples;
I will sing praises to You among the nations.

10For Your loyal love is great, reaching to the heavens,
and Your truth to the clouds.

11Be exalted above the heavens, God;
let Your glory be over all the earth.

Notes

  • The title "Do Not Destroy… in the cave" — al tashchet, perhaps a tune (58; 59; 75); the cave is Adullam or the cave at En-gedi, where David spared Saul (1 Samuel 22:1; 24:3).

  • v1 "in the shadow of Your wings" — as in 17:8 and 36:7; the storms of ruin, havvot.

  • v3 "God will send out His loyal love and His truth" — chesed and emet as God's messengers sent to rescue (43:3).

  • v4 "those who blaze" — lohatim, men aflame with hatred, like fire-breathing beasts. Their tongue a sharp sword (55:21; 64:3).

  • vv5, 11 — the refrain, the same in both places.

  • v6 "they have fallen into it themselves" — as in 7:15 and 9:15.

  • vv7–11 — repeated as the first half of Psalm 108 (108:1–5).

  • v8 "I will wake the dawn" — the singer rises before the sun to praise God, waking the morning instead of being woken by it.

I call to God Most High, to God who completes His work for me.
He will send from heaven and save me; He puts to shame the one who tramples on me. Selah God will send out His loyal love and His truth.

chapters.title: Surely There Is a God Who Judges
chapters.html:
Psalms 58

For the director: "Do Not Destroy." Of David. A Miktam.

1Do you indeed speak righteousness, you gods?
Do you judge the children of man uprightly?

2No, in your heart you work injustice;
on the earth you weigh out the violence of your hands.

3The wicked go astray from the womb;
they err from birth, speaking lies.

4They have venom like the venom of a snake,
like the deaf cobra that stops its ear,

5that does not hear the voice of the charmers
or the skilled caster of spells.

6God, break the teeth in their mouth;
tear out the fangs of the young lions, LORD.

7Let them melt away like water that runs off;
when he bends his arrows, let them be cut off.

8Let them be like the snail that dissolves as it goes,
like a woman's stillborn child, that never sees the sun.

9Before your pots feel the thorns,
whether green or burning, He will sweep them away.

10The righteous will rejoice when he sees the vengeance;
he will wash his feet in the blood of the wicked.

11Mankind will say, "Surely there is fruit for the righteous;
surely there is a God who judges on the earth."

Notes

  • v1 "you gods" — the Hebrew has elem, silence; read with other vowels as elim, gods, the rulers and judges who were to give justice in God's name (82:1, 6; Exodus 21:6). The Greek reads if indeed you speak righteousness.

  • v2 "you weigh out the violence of your hands" — judges who use the scales of justice to measure out injustice.

  • vv4–5 "the deaf cobra… the charmers" — a snake that will not be charmed, as the wicked will not listen (Jeremiah 8:17; Ecclesiastes 10:11).

  • v6 "break the teeth in their mouth" — the wicked as lions, as in 3:7.

  • vv7–9 — images of passing away: water soaking into the ground, a snail's trail, a stillborn child, thorns burned up under a pot before it heats. The Hebrew of vv7 and 9 is very hard, and the readings are uncertain.

  • v10 "he will wash his feet in the blood of the wicked" — the language of total victory in battle (68:23; Isaiah 63:3); the psalm cries for God's justice, not private revenge (Romans 12:19).

  • v11 "Surely there is a God who judges on the earth" — Elohim shofetim: the answer to the unjust gods of v1.

Mankind will say, "Surely there is fruit for the righteous; surely there is a God who judges on the earth."

chapters.title: God Is My Stronghold
chapters.html:
Psalms 59

For the director: "Do Not Destroy." Of David. A Miktam, when Saul sent men, and they watched the house to kill him.

1Deliver me from my enemies, my God;
set me on high, away from those who rise against me.

2Deliver me from those who do iniquity,
and save me from men of bloodshed.

3For they lie in wait for my life;
fierce men stir up strife against me,
not for my transgression or my sin, LORD.

4For no guilt of mine they run and make ready;
wake up to meet me, and see.

5You, LORD God of hosts, the God of Israel,
rouse Yourself to punish all the nations;
show no grace to any of the treacherous who do iniquity. Selah

6They return at evening;
they howl like dogs
and go around the city.

7They pour out words with their mouths;
swords are in their lips,
"for who hears?"

8But You, LORD, laugh at them;
You mock all the nations.

9My strength, I will watch for You,
for God is my stronghold.

10The God of my loyal love will come to meet me;
God will let me look on those who watch me.

11Do not kill them, or my people will forget;
make them wander by Your power and bring them down,
Lord, our shield.

12For the sin of their mouth, the word of their lips,
let them be caught in their pride,
for the cursing and the lies they tell.

13Consume them in wrath;
consume them till they are no more,
so that they may know that God rules in Jacob
to the ends of the earth. Selah

14They return at evening;
they howl like dogs
and go around the city.

15They wander about for food,
and if they are not satisfied, they stay all night.

16But I will sing of Your strength;
I will shout for joy at Your loyal love in the morning,
for You have been a stronghold for me
and a refuge in the day of my distress.

17My strength, I will sing praises to You,
for God is my stronghold,
the God of my loyal love.

Notes

  • The title — Michal let David down through a window when Saul's men watched his house by night (1 Samuel 19:11–17).

  • v3 "fierce men stir up strife" — yaguru, the second gur, to attack, as in 56:6.

  • v5 "LORD God of hosts, the God of Israel" — YHWH Elohim tseva'ot, a rare gathering of names; the enemies are called the nations, perhaps because the psalm was later used against foreign foes.

  • vv6, 14 — the refrain: the enemies as the half-wild dogs that roamed city streets at night, scavenging (1 Kings 14:11).

  • v9 "My strength" — the Hebrew has uzzo, his strength; the Greek and some Hebrew manuscripts read uzzi, my strength, as in v17, followed here.

  • v10 "The God of my loyal love" — the read form, Elohei chasdi, as in v17, followed here; the written form has chasdo, the God of His loyal love.

  • v11 "Do not kill them, or my people will forget" — let the enemies live, scattered, as a lasting lesson of God's judgment.

  • vv16–17 — the morning song answers the evening howling (vv6, 14): night belongs to the dogs, the morning to God's loyal love (30:5).

chapters.title: With God We Will Do Valiantly
chapters.html:
Psalms 60

For the director: on "The Lily of Testimony." A Miktam of David, to teach; when he fought with Aram-naharaim and Aram-zobah, and Joab returned and struck down twelve thousand of Edom in the Valley of Salt.

1God, You have rejected us; You have broken us;
You have been angry; restore us.

2You have made the land quake; You have split it open;
heal its breaches, for it totters.

3You have made Your people see hard things;
You have given us wine to drink that makes us reel.

4You have given a banner to those who fear You,
to rally to it because of the bow. Selah

5So that Your beloved ones may be rescued,
save with Your right hand, and answer me.

6God has spoken in His holiness:
"I will exult; I will divide Shechem
and measure out the Valley of Succoth.

7Gilead is Mine, and Manasseh is Mine;
Ephraim is the helmet of My head;
Judah is My scepter.

8Moab is My washbasin;
on Edom I throw My sandal;
Philistia, shout in triumph over Me!"

9Who will bring me to the fortified city?
Who will lead me to Edom?

10Have You not rejected us, God?
You do not go out, God, with our armies.

11Give us help against the foe,
for the salvation of man is worthless.

12With God we will do valiantly,
and He will trample our foes.

Notes

  • The title — David's wars against the Arameans and Edom (2 Samuel 8:3–14; 1 Chronicles 18:3–13). The Hebrew title takes two verses. To teach may mean it was to be learned by heart (Deuteronomy 31:19; 2 Samuel 1:18).

  • vv1–3 — a lament after a defeat, perhaps an Edomite raid while the army was away in the north.

  • v3 "wine… that makes us reel" — yayin tar'elah, the cup of God's wrath (75:8; Isaiah 51:17).

  • v4 "because of the bow" — mipnei qoshet, which may mean to flee from the bow, or, from another root, for the sake of truth; the Greek has from before the bow.

  • v5 "answer me" — the read form; the written form has answer us.

  • vv6–8 — God's oracle, dividing the land as its owner: Shechem west of the Jordan and Succoth east of it; Gilead and Manasseh; Ephraim and Judah as His helmet and scepter. Moab is a mere washbasin, Edom the slave to whom He throws His sandal (Ruth 4:7).

  • v8 "Philistia, shout in triumph over Me!" — a challenge; Psalm 108:9 has over Philistia I shout in triumph.

  • vv5–12 — repeated as the second half of Psalm 108 (108:6–13).

  • v11 "the salvation of man is worthless" — shav teshu'at adam (146:3).

chapters.title: The Rock That Is Higher Than I
chapters.html:
Psalms 61

For the director: on a stringed instrument. Of David.

1Hear my cry, God;
listen to my prayer.

2From the end of the earth I call to You
when my heart grows faint;
lead me to the rock that is higher than I,

3for You have been a refuge for me,
a strong tower against the enemy.

4Let me live as a guest in Your tent forever;
let me take refuge in the shelter of Your wings. Selah

5For You, God, have heard my vows;
You have given me the inheritance of those who fear Your name.

6Add days to the days of the king;
may his years be as generation after generation.

7May he sit enthroned forever before God;
appoint loyal love and truth to keep him.

8So I will sing praise to Your name forever,
as I pay my vows day after day.

Notes

  • v2 "From the end of the earth" — far from Jerusalem, whether in exile or in flight; or at the edge of Sheol (Jonah 2:2–4).

  • v2 "the rock that is higher than I" — a refuge the psalmist cannot climb by himself; God must lead him up to it.

  • v4 "Let me live as a guest in Your tent forever" — agurah, from gur, as the word table has it (15:1; 27:4–5).

  • v4 "the shelter of Your wings" — as in 17:8 and 57:1.

  • vv6–7 "Add days to the days of the king" — a prayer for the king in the middle of the psalm (21:4); if David is the speaker, he prays for himself in the third person.

  • v7 "appoint loyal love and truth to keep him" — chesed and emet, God's guards for the king (40:11; 57:3).

Hear my cry, God; listen to my prayer.
From the end of the earth I call to You when my heart grows faint; lead me to the rock that is higher than I,
for You have been a refuge for me, a strong tower against the enemy.
Let me live as a guest in Your tent forever; let me take refuge in the shelter of Your wings. Selah
For You, God, have heard my vows; You have given me the inheritance of those who fear Your name.
Add days to the days of the king; may his years be as generation after generation.
May he sit enthroned forever before God; appoint loyal love and truth to keep him.
So I will sing praise to Your name forever, as I pay my vows day after day.

chapters.title: My Soul Waits in Silence
chapters.html:
Psalms 62

For the director: for Jeduthun. A psalm of David.

1For God alone my soul waits in silence;
from Him comes my salvation.

2He alone is my rock and my salvation,
my stronghold; I will not be greatly moved.

3How long will you rush at a man,
all of you, to batter him down,
like a leaning wall, a tottering fence?

4They only plan to push him down from his high place;
they take pleasure in lies.
They bless with their mouth,
but inwardly they curse. Selah

5For God alone, my soul, wait in silence,
for my hope is from Him.

6He alone is my rock and my salvation,
my stronghold; I will not be moved.

7On God rests my salvation and my glory;
my rock of strength, my refuge is in God.

8Trust in Him at all times, you people;
pour out your heart before Him;
God is a refuge for us. Selah

9The sons of men are only a breath;
the sons of men of rank are a lie;
in the scales they go up;
together they are lighter than a breath.

10Do not trust in oppression,
and put no empty hope in robbery;
if wealth increases, do not set your heart on it.

11God has spoken once;
twice I have heard this:
that power belongs to God,

12and loyal love belongs to You, Lord;
for You repay a man according to his work.

Notes

  • The psalm — akh, only, alone, surely, begins six of its lines (vv1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 9): God alone is to be trusted.

  • vv1, 5 "For God alone my soul waits in silence" — the refrain, slightly varied: v1 dumiyyah, silence, a statement; v5 dommi, be silent, the soul told to wait.

  • vv2, 6 — the second refrain: I will not be greatly moved (v2) becomes I will not be moved (v6).

  • v3 "like a leaning wall, a tottering fence" — the enemies attack one already near falling.

  • v8 "pour out your heart before Him" — shifkhu, as water poured out (1 Samuel 1:15; Lamentations 2:19).

  • v9 "The sons of men… the sons of men of rank" — benei adam and benei ish, the common people and the great: put on God's scales, both together weigh less than a breath, hevel (39:5).

  • v10 "if wealth increases, do not set your heart on it" — as in 49:16–17 and 1 Timothy 6:17.

  • vv11–12 "God has spoken once; twice I have heard this" — the counting saying of wisdom (Job 33:14; Proverbs 6:16): power and loyal love both belong to God. You repay a man according to his work is quoted in Romans 2:6.

chapters.title: My Soul Thirsts for You
chapters.html:
Psalms 63

A psalm of David, when he was in the wilderness of Judah.

1God, You are my God; I seek You early;
my soul thirsts for You;
my flesh longs for You,
in a dry and weary land without water.

2So I have looked on You in the sanctuary,
seeing Your power and Your glory.

3Because Your loyal love is better than life,
my lips will praise You.

4So I will bless You as long as I live;
in Your name I will lift up my hands.

5My soul will be satisfied as with fat and rich food,
and my mouth will praise You with joyful lips,

6when I remember You on my bed
and meditate on You in the watches of the night;

7for You have been my help,
and in the shadow of Your wings I sing for joy.

8My soul clings to You;
Your right hand holds me up.

9But those who seek my life to destroy it
will go down into the depths of the earth;

10they will be handed over to the power of the sword;
they will be a portion for jackals.

11But the king will rejoice in God;
all who swear by Him will boast,
for the mouths of those who speak lies will be stopped.

Notes

  • The title "in the wilderness of Judah" — David fleeing from Saul (1 Samuel 23:14) or from Absalom (2 Samuel 15:23–28).

  • v1 "I seek You early" — ashachareka, from shachar, dawn: to seek at daybreak, and so earnestly. The Church has long sung the psalm at the morning prayer.

  • v1 "a dry and weary land without water" — the desert outside, and the thirst of the soul within (42:1–2; 143:6).

  • v2 "So I have looked on You in the sanctuary" — the memory of worship in the house of God sustains him in the desert.

  • v3 "Your loyal love is better than life" — chesed above life itself.

  • v6 "the watches of the night" — the night was divided into three watches (Judges 7:19; Lamentations 2:19).

  • v7 "the shadow of Your wings" — as in 17:8, 36:7, 57:1 and 61:4.

  • v8 "My soul clings to You" — daveqah, the word for a man holding fast to his wife (Genesis 2:24) and Israel to God (Deuteronomy 10:20).

  • v10 "a portion for jackals" — shu'alim, jackals or foxes, the scavengers of the battlefield.

  • v11 "all who swear by Him" — by God, or by the king's life (1 Samuel 17:55); the psalm ends with the king, as Psalm 61 does.
